_datum: Origin = the INSIDE CORNER of the bench top, where the main table and the return meet and where both walls meet. Everything is positive from there. +x runs along the RETURN, away from the back wall, toward where you stand (0..133.5). +y runs along the MAIN TABLE, away from the return corner (0..82). +z is up off the table top; below the bench is -z.
_why_x_is_the_return: Handedness, not preference. From the corner the main table goes one way and the return the other. Putting +x along the MAIN table and +y along the return gives x cross y = -z, a LEFT-handed frame, which silently mirrors the whole cell - that exact mistake was made once already on 2026-07-26 and only the 3D render caught it. Assigning +x to the return and +y to the main table gives x cross y = +z. Verified in code, not assumed.
_measured: 2026-07-26, Kyle. Unmeasured values are null ON PURPOSE - the twin models only what is measured and reports the rest as absent, because a guessed obstacle is worse than a missing one (the gate would report CLEAR against a fiction).

surfaces.name: main
surfaces.notes: The main run. 27.5 deep from the back wall (+x), 82 long from the return corner (+y).

surfaces.name: return
surfaces.notes: The return, 20.25 wide, running out along +x. From the back wall it is 27.5 (the main depth) + 34 = 61.5 to the seam, then 72 more, so 133.5 total - this surface covers x 27.5..133.5.

_walls_note: `height` is the wall's real height above the TABLE TOP. `usable_height`, when present, is how far up is actually reachable - the return side is limited to 34 by ceiling ducts even though the wall itself runs to 48-7/8. Keep them separate: collapsing them would move the wall face the moment someone measures the duct properly. yaw_deg is the direction the wall RUNS (0 = along +x, 90 = along +y); outward is which way the wall MATERIAL sits from its face.

walls.name: back
walls.notes: The MAIN TABLE's back wall, running along +y at x=0, 5 in thick (material occupies x -5..0). 48-7/8 above the table, MEASURED. Starts 8.25 out from the side wall, leaving the corner gap at y 0..8.25. Extends DOWN below the table to its footing; the bottom edge follows the sloping floor. Carries the shelf.

walls.name: side
walls.notes: The RETURN's wall, running along +x at y=0. PHYSICALLY the same 48-7/8 as the main back wall; the 34 is USABLE space, cut short by ceiling-mount ducts above the return. Modelled as the true wall plus a usable_height limit rather than as a short wall, because a duct is an overhead obstacle, not a lower wall face.

corner_gap._comment: Gap where the back wall meets the side wall. MEASURED 2026-07-26 at 8.25, so the back wall spans y 8.25..82 and the gap is y 0..8.25.

_legs_note: THE TABLE TOP IS LEVEL AND THE FLOOR IS NOT, so the legs are the only measurement of the floor: differing heights ARE the slope, and the floor plane is solved from them rather than stored - so leg POSITIONS matter as much as heights. x/y are the leg station's CENTRE. `height` is TRUSS HEIGHT: floor to the UNDERSIDE of the table top, excluding the 3/4 top. It is NOT the cut length of a single 2x4 (Kyle, 2026-07-26) - the truss is legs plus rails and no one piece is that long. Do not hand these numbers to a saw. The distinction does not affect the floor: floor-to-underside is exactly what the plane needs. Nominal lumber is not actual lumber: a 2x4 is 1.5 x 3.5.

legs.name: main_outside_corner
legs.notes: Outside (front) corner of the main table at its far end, INSET from both edges - the top overhangs the frame. Inset of 1.0 is an ESTIMATE from the photo, not a measurement. Part of a 4-piece 2x4 truss with main_near_back_wall. MEASURED truss height.

legs.name: main_near_back_wall
legs.notes: Far end of the main table, the leg by the back wall. It stands RIGHT IN FRONT OF the footing, not inside it - its back face is on the footing's front face at x=7, so its centre is x 7.75. Part of a 4-piece 2x4 truss with main_outside_corner. MEASURED truss height.

legs.name: return_seam
legs.notes: At the return's seam, 61.5 from the back wall. MEASURED truss height. Inset 1.0 from the return's outer edge on the same ESTIMATE. ASSUMPTION: it is on the outer edge rather than against the wall or centred - that choice tilts the solved floor plane, so correct it if wrong.

foundations.name: main_wall
foundations.notes: Concrete footing straddling the main table's back wall: 7 into the room, the wall's 5 thickness, then 7 behind - 19 total. 9 tall, sitting FLUSH on the floor, so it inherits the floor's 2.45 deg tilt rather than being a level block with a gap at one end.

fixtures.name: main_backwall_shelf
fixtures.notes: Protrudes from the MAIN TABLE back wall. 50.75 long (exact) along +y, 8 deep (Kyle's estimate) out along +x. Inset ~5 from the main table's far end (y=82), so it spans y 26.25..77 - ASSUMPTION about which edge 'inset 5 from the edge of the table' meant. Its UNDERSIDE HEIGHT above the table is NOT MEASURED, so it is not rendered or gated. Frame is half-cut 2x4: a beam along the wall at the shelf's back edge with two sides cut at 45 degrees; those brackets hang BELOW the shelf and are what the arm would strike first, so the slab alone would be optimistic.

features.name: return_seam
features.notes: Where the return's two tops meet, 61.5 from the back wall (27.5 + 34). The return_seam leg lands here.

features.name: return_ceiling_ducts
features.notes: Ceiling-mounted ducts above the RETURN. Not measured, so not modelled - their only recorded effect is the side wall's usable_height of 34. When measured they become a fixture with kind 'duct' (geom group 3, toggleable in the viewer).

features.name: return_wall_foundation
features.notes: A HIGH concrete foundation runs along the return wall, taller than the main wall's. Not measured yet - Kyle said to estimate it later. Deliberately absent rather than guessed.

features.name: floor_drain
features.notes: A drain is visible in the floor photo, consistent with the 2.45 deg slab tilt the leg lengths imply. Not modelled; noted because it explains the slope.

arm._comment: Where the arm's base centre sits on the table, in datum coords, and which way it faces. yaw_deg is the direction the arm points with m1 at 0 deg: 0 = along +x, positive counter-clockwise viewed from above. SAFETY-CRITICAL: switching the twin from its infinite ground plane to the real finite tabletop makes the gate LESS conservative - it will believe there is air past the table edge. A wrong arm position therefore means the gate can call CLEAR over real tabletop. Until x/y/yaw_deg are measured the twin keeps the infinite plane.

_view_note: Saved free-camera pose from the last --view session (MuJoCo units, metres). Restored on the next --view and used by --render. Delete this key to go back to the derived angles.
_truss_note: Legs sharing a `truss` name are one braced frame - Kyle's photo shows the far end of the main table as a 4-piece 2x4 truss: two legs, a top rail under the table top, and a bottom rail at the floor. The rails are DERIVED from the leg pair rather than listed, so moving a leg cannot leave its rails behind. ESTIMATE: the bottom rail is placed with its underside on the floor; measure its real height if it matters.
